report.scope: Six program forms compute the same Rosenbrock descent and complete final vector. A seventh timing entry is a byte-identical copy of fwp-packed under a different filename. Its timing ratio is a control for differences unrelated to executable contents. Fourteen-round blocks balance every execution position and ordered adjacent pair within rounds; block row order is shuffled with the explicit recorded seed. Cross-round boundaries are not balanced. fwp-ad records and reverses derivatives; the other five use the explicit derivative. Comparing fwp-ad to a peer includes general AD work and representation costs, not pure compiler overhead. fwp-explicit uses immutable lists and intermediate pairs/lists; fwp-packed generates a packed array per update, reading the previous array at checked indices. fwp-packed-baseline recompiles the accepted generated C without the stack-array field move. C/Rust reuse two contiguous buffers. Explicit formulas preserve their multiplication order, but reverse AD may round differently. All outputs are checked against an independent Python derivative with absolute/relative tolerance 1e-10. Per-implementation timed outputs must repeat exactly. Inputs and update counts are compile-time constants. C/Rust/fwp formatting and allocation strategies differ. Timings include fresh-process startup, initialization, descent, complete output and teardown; compilation and instrumentation are excluded. The zero-update case includes initialization and formatting, so it is not pure startup time. Raw derivative buffers and managed charge are observed separately for fwp only. Separate uninstrumented process RSS includes all process storage; do not add it to allocation peaks. The recompiled packed baseline must reproduce its recorded managed/raw profile exactly. Current fwp forms must preserve allocation requests/bytes and raw storage, without increasing retains or managed peak. At least 199 updates must reduce packed retains. All timing peers are rebuilt and measured together. All samples, compile commands and GCC static frame estimates are retained. Frame estimates are not peak stack use and do not cover Rust. No speed threshold is claimed.
